task: We have got a mission for you, ranger <Ranger>. As you know the larger part of our home planet of <FromPlanet> is covered with huge blue oceans. They are the bluest and the largest in this whole Galaxy! Due to that we would often research the depths of the oceans and our experts are really the best in this field. So, the government of planet <ToPlanet> in the  <ToStar> system, asked us to send them a diving expert whom they need to do some work at the bottom of an ocean. They've encountered some sort of a problem there and they need help from experienced rescue divers. We would like to help them, but the problem is our men are always occupied. Since piloting a submarine ship is much easier than a spaceship, we could charge this mission to you. If you succeed you could earn yourself a round sum of <Money> cr and the gratitude of the local government. You must come to the planet of <ToPlanet> not later than <Date>. So, what do you say?
success: Thank you so much, ranger <Ranger>! You successfully accomplished the mission not failing our reputation as leaders of submarine research! Please accept the promised fee of <Money> cr.
loc.3.0:
- Well, up to you, might as well do without you... 

You returned back to the spaceport. Mission failed.
loc.8.0:
- Excellent. You can head for the "Mermaid" naval base straight away. You will dive from there. Our people will escort you.

Half an hour later you were already approaching the naval base that was peacefully drifting on the ocean waves. Onboard of the Mermaid you were met by a cheerful captain, and by the looks on his face one could think that it was him who was going to dive.

- We have been waiting for you, - he shouted, trying to out-shout the wind. - The apparatus has been carefully inspected, it is fully operable. We sure do hope that you - as a diving expert - will be able to help us. Let us proceed to my deckhouse.

You decided not to upset the captain by telling him who you really were. Inside the deckhouse it was quiet and cosy. Cattle filled with some sort of a green liquid buzzed peacefully on the optrone furnace. You remembered about the coming dive onto the bottom of the cold ocean and shivered. But it was too late to refuse, - after all, you were a ranger, not some spoiled brat?

- The unidentified object fell not far from the <clr>south-western<clrEnd> coast, - the captain said - its co-ordinates are X=[p8] and Y=[p9]. The object lies approximately in the <clr>middle of a plateau<clrEnd> [p6] by [p6] meters in size, at the depth of [p11] meters. Your objective is to <clr>dive on the plateau, find the object and take it with your gripper.<clrEnd>.

There are constant submarine currents in the coastal waters of this area. They will be pushing you bathyscaph to the side, so you should make a current adjustment while piloting the apparatus. Watch your gauges for direction and speed of the currents when diving. You have a <clr>90 minute<clrEnd> oxygen reserve to stay underwater. While you are underwater we will be keeping a constant connection with you. Any questions?
loc.8.1: The display of your onboard hydro-locator will be showing the distance to target in two co-ordinates <clr>by X and Y axis<clrEnd>. At that <clr>you bathyscaph shall be considered as zero-co-ordinate<clrEnd>. For instance not it shows X=[p8] and Y=[p9]. Which means the target is located at the distance of [p8] meters <clr>to the east<clrEnd> and [p9] meters <clr>to the north<clrEnd> of us.
loc.8.2: The display of your onboard hydro-locator will be showing the distance to target in two co-ordinates <clr>by X and Y axis<clrEnd>. At that <clr>you bathyscaph shall be considered as zero-co-ordinate<clrEnd>. For instance not it shows X=[p8] and Y=[p9]. Which means the target is located at the distance of {-[p8]} meters <clr>to the west<clrEnd> and [p9] meters <clr>to the north<clrEnd> of us.

Which means the target is located at the distance of [p8] meters <clr>to the east<clrEnd> and {-[p9]} meters <clr>to the south<clrEnd> of us.
loc.8.4: The display of your onboard hydro-locator will be showing the distance to target in two co-ordinates <clr>by X and Y axis<clrEnd>. At that <clr>you bathyscaph shall be considered as zero-co-ordinate<clrEnd>. For instance not it shows X=[p8] and Y=[p9]. Which means the target is located at the distance of {-[p8]} meters <clr>to the west<clrEnd> and {-[p9]} meters <clr>to the south <clrEnd> of us.
loc.8.5:
The object lies at the depth of [p11] meters from the waterline. I must say we are lucky. The space alien stopped on a small horizontal plateau, located on a vertical slope of a rock. If it had not been for that, it could have dropped much deeper, the depth of the nearest cavity is some 10,000 meters! 

Now, here are the details of the local submarine relief. In the southern direction the slope of the underwater rock has a grade of [p1] meters for each 10 meters, while in the western direction it is [p2] meters for each 10 meters. The object lies approximately in the middle of a <clr>plateau<clrEnd>, having [p6] by [p6] meters in size. Your sonic depth finder will be constantly tracking the depth of the oceans in each your location. The barometer will help you determine the diving depth. Do not forget to look at your display board, or else you will crash to the bottom!
loc.8.6: - Simply <clr>turn on the searchlights<clrEnd>. The object is quite large so you must spot it at once.
loc.8.7:
Judging by the look that the captain gave you, his opinion of you had just started dropping. Nonetheless he answered:

- First of all you must <clr>land on the plateau<clrEnd>. This means that <clr>both of the co-ordinates<clrEnd> must be within the span of {-[p6]/2} through {[p6]/2}, and <clr>your diving depth<clrEnd> must be about [p11] metres (It is better if you actually land on the bottom, although you can still drift over it at the height of no less than <clr>10 metres<clrEnd> or else the gripper will not work). Then you should <clr>turn on the searchlights<clrEnd>, find the object and take it with your gripper. After that you can surface. Crystal?
loc.12.0: In front of you, you saw the bathyscaph control knobs and the instrumentation display. What are you going to do next?
loc.15.0:
The bathyscaph was located on the front deck and was ready for the dive. Inside it was very cozy. That is aside from the fact that you could only turn one foot at a time and not more than by 30 degrees, everything was more or less fine. The tools were blinking with coloured lights and unintelligible numbers. Huge view-ports were located on the left, right and central sides of the hull. You sealed the hitch, and several minutes later the apparatus jerked and rolled to the side. Apparently the dive had begun. You put on the headphones with a microphone. 
- This is <Ranger>. Over.
- This is captain of the Mermaid - you heard in response. - How is it going? 
- Excellent! Never been better! Over, - you tried to speak with maximum sarcasm but apparently the captain did not notice it. 
- Good! We are releasing the grips. 
You felt a jolt, and the apparatus, which you had already nicknamed "Kid", started its slow descend into the blue abyss. The adventure has begun!..
- Break a leg, <Ranger>!
loc.18.0: How much do you intend to drop?
loc.21.0: You looked down at the no-contact sensor panel with arrow buttons, pointing in all four directions. The buttons were lit from the back with neon lights. Make your choice! Where do you want to turn?
loc.27.0:
You popped up on the surface like a cork out of the bottle!
The Mermaid rescue boat drifted nearby. When you climbed out of the bathyscaph, everyone who was in the boat started hugging and congratulating you. The captain's hugs were most hearty. You even started suspecting it could be something completely different. 
As soon as the captain broke away from you he said: 
- You managed to deliver the capsule very quickly, it continues emitting signals, and, it looks like, there is a living organism inside! During the climb the capsule has apparently noted the change in the outside pressure, because the emitted signals became stronger! For such a brilliant accomplishment of your mission we will pay you a bonus of <clr>2000<clrEnd> cr in addition to the sum that you've been promised. Congratulations, mate! How about a small celebration?
- No, thank you, I am in a big hurry, - you refused politely and shook the captain's hand, trying to simultaneously figure out how much money you now had in your account. Looks like it was closing, [p24] cr... 
The scientists quickly loaded the unusual space capsule on board of the boat, pulled your iron friend out of the water and headed for the naval base. 
Mission accomplished successfully!
loc.27.1:
You popped up on the surface like a cork out of the bottle!
The Mermaid rescue boat drifted nearby. When you climbed out of the bathyscaph, everyone who was in the boat started hugging and congratulating you. The captain's hugs were most hearty. You even started suspecting it could be something completely different. 
The scientists carefully loaded the unusual space capsule on board of the boat, pulled your iron friend out of the water and headed for the naval base. 
Mission accomplished successfully!
loc.31.0:
You popped up on the surface like a cork out of the bottle!
The Mermaid rescue boat drifted nearby. You climbed out of the bathyscaph and took a deep breath of fresh air. "Am I really still alive? - you thought looking at the blue sky of planet <ToPlanet>. - Next time I should take a cat with me - must be fun!" 
You greeted the captain and headed for the boat. Your submarine experience did you a lot of good, although you failed your mission.
loc.36.0: Suddenly the siren went off, and you noticed traces of water run down the illuminators. The same second you head started aching, the pressure was growing quickly. Last thing you remembered before you passed out was your home...
loc.37.0:
Apparently the cold season has begun on planet <ToPlanet>. As you marched towards the government house you felt the freezing wind pierce right through you. The small annoying rain would stop and start back again. All of that coupled with the gloomy and grey skies was really dragging your spirits down. 
In the secret operations department you saw an officer, who was sitting behind a massive plastic desk of strictly official design. 
- Will they ever send us whom we have actually been asking for?! - the secret service representative hissed under his breath barely giving you a brief glance. - We were asking for a diving expert, and once again they are sending some ranger! Apparently, they think, that the space rangers are you jacks-of-all-trades! 
With these words the officer turned away in irritation and stared at the window. 
- Alright, I will explain the problem to you, and you see for yourself if you are going to take upon it or not. Chances are we do not have much time, so you probably could get this mission. 
The arrogant tone of the officer was starting to get on your nerves. Are they doubting your expertise?
- Just recently, a strange space object of unknown origin entered the atmosphere of our planet. Upon re-entry it caught fire, after which the object followed a strange trajectory into the ocean and sank. The object emits signals, and was apparently produced b y intelligent creatures. Quite possibly it is a capsule containing a transmitter or maybe even a living creature signalling May-Day! In any event, we want to recover this object for further studying. So that's your objective! You will dive to the bottom of the ocean in a special submarine apparatus codename R I-00-M, grip the object and carry it to the surface. Any questions?
loc.37.1:
- This a bathyscaph for deep dives. Unfortunately I do not understand much about these submarine apparatuses. Here is the documentation - take your time to study it. I'll go have some coffee. 
With these words the officer handed you three enormous volumes of the technical documentation to the R I-00-M submersible and stepped out of the room. You began your reading.
The first volume was reserved for the statement of warranty by the manufacturer, proudly named "Pantel", whose headquarters were located somewhere on the Lost Islands. The apparatus was designed at the special order of the OpSec Service. From this first volume you also found out that aside from R I-00-M, they also developed another model codename R I-00-F, which had a larger diving depth. There was also a later development of the bathyscaph - R II-00 - but it did not differ from the previous two in any way, aside from an improved design and triple-price.
The second volume contained the list of possible failures and methods of their fixing. It should be noted that this volume was a lot thicker than the rest. 
The third and the last volume was the most important one for you, since it contained the information on the <clr>principles of operating and navigation methods<clrEnd>. The R I apparatuses were equipped with a <clr>handler-gripper<clrEnd>, intended for recovering load from the sea bottom, as well as for taking samples of water and ground. Its hull was made of special extra-strong alloys, capable of resisting high pressures in the thick of the water, as well as collisions against the ground with a speed of up to <clr>100<clrEnd> meters per minute. The maximum diving depth of R I-00-M is {([p11] div 500 + 1) * 500} meters.
The apparatus is propelled with an engine, the technicalities of which you decided to skip, only noticing that its maximum horizontal speed was <clr>100 meters per min<clrEnd>, while the current speed of the bathyscaph could be increased at the rate of <clr>10 meters per minutes<clrEnd>. In order to manoeuvre you can easily turn the bathyscaph around its vertical axis. Diving is facilitated through the use of ballast, dropping off which you could reduce the vertical speed of the dive and finally surface. The initial ballast weight is <clr>1300 kg<clrEnd>, which provides a diving speed of approximately <clr>300 meters per minute<clrEnd>. If you drop <clr>300 kg<clrEnd> of ballast, the apparatus will stop diving. Further ballast drop will cause the apparatus to surface. 
This volume also contained safety recommendations, but at that moment the secret operations department chief went in and interrupted your reading. 
- Any other questions?
loc.37.2: - Well... I think that a daredevil fighter that you should not fear anything, should he now? - the officer winked. - However if we are talking dangers, I think, you should be aware of the following... Do not stay underwater too long - your oxygen reserve is limited. You can also collide against the bottom or underwater riffs, if you dive too fast or in the wrong direction (a collision may damage the apparatus). Also, certain emergency situations are possible... But I hope it's going to be okay. Anything else?
jump.15.text: No more questions, sir. I am ready to dive
jump.20.desc: The engine was located right under you. You felt its even buzz increase.
jump.21.desc: You pulled the control lever further back. The back thrust increased. Now you had adjust to underwater currents and go to your point of destination.
jump.23.desc: This wasn't too difficult. Somewhere on the right a turbine started buzzing. The bathyscaph turned slowly to the right direction.
jump.25.desc:
- May-Day, May-Day! - you screamed hysterically into the transmitter. 
- What happened? Over, - you heard the worried voice of the captain.
jump.31.desc: You turned on the searchlights, and a bright ray of light broke through the thick of the water. The light power was enough to see several meters ahead. You noticed some movement in front of the illuminators. Small molluscs danced gaily in the beams of artificial light. Some of these funny living organisms looked like wiggling worms, while other were more on the round side and bore a slight resemblance to small octopuses. You couldn't but admire at this underwater miracle!
jump.33.text: I don't know what to do. This damn iron tin just wouldn't listen to me!
jump.33.desc:
- Did you read the documentation? Over, - the captain asked.
- I don't remember. Over.
- Are you a diver or what? Over, - you could hear a shade of doubt in the captain's voice.
- Oh yes. Got it, sorry to bother you. Over.
- Excellent. Continue the mission. Over and out.
jump.42.desc: Feeling a slight bump you understood that another portion of the unnecessary cargo was dropped. The "Kid" rocked softly. Now the dive speed is going to be slower.
jump.44.desc: You felt a buzz right under your seat. You imagined the fans of the back turbine increase their momentum. The bathyscaph shuddered. You estimated the co-ordinates in which you would be within a minute, considering the engine thrust. A minute passed, but the hydro-locator showed different co-ordinates. Maybe you should have made an adjustment for the current?
jump.45.desc: You pushed the speed lever forward will full force. Judging by the buzz that came from beyond the fans now revolved slower.
jump.46.desc: The engine noise went quieter and quieter until the fans of the back turbine finally stopped. Now your small ship was fully in the powers of underwater currents.
jump.47.desc: You decided to move back. The engine roared. Did they forget to get a silencer on this thing?
jump.48.desc: Pulling the lever you heard the engine go silent. It became very quiet and the feeling of loneliness together with tons of water over your head overwhelmed you. The horrifying wait began.
jump.49.desc: In order to stop the engine you had to slightly pull the main lever. The turbines stopped. The engine went silent. What next? Your "Kid" was now fully in the power of the currents.
jump.50.desc: You decided to reduce the main thrust. One move, and the engine buzz became quieter. The back fan flapping reduced.
jump.52.desc: The bathyscaph obediently turned in the required direction. You felt like a real submariner. Even the great Jab Hick Gusto from the planet of Gargyng could not dream of anything like this!
jump.53.desc: Pushing the up-arrow button you felt the turbine buzz somewhere on the left. The bathyscaph obediently turned in the required direction.
jump.54.desc: Rotating around the vertical axis, you thought of home. Somewhere far away now, emerald gardens bloomed and visitant birds made their nests. "Why am I remembering my past?! Isn't that a bad superstition?" - you thought and looked out of the window. "Do not let yourself lose the grip!" - you cheered yourself.
jump.55.desc: Judging by your own calculations, you were moving in the right direction. Now you just had to wait for the "Kid" to arrive to the point of destination. You leaned back in the chair and let yourself go, sipping on a glass of brandy, thoughtfully left by the previous pilot under the seat.
jump.59.desc: You small ship was rushing down with enormous speed. You saw a blur of underwater creatures pass by. The diving speed was so high, you couldn't even make out what you saw. At times you'd hear something bump on the hull, most likely it were the fish who didn't have the time to swim out of the way. It was quickly growing dark. A black abyss opened its endless mouth beyond!..
jump.61.desc: You've noticed the first raise of light from above. You were gradually reaching the surface!
jump.62.desc: Suddenly you felt a strong hit! The bathyscaph boomed and stood motionless. Looks like you hit the ocean bottom! The collision was so powerful you glanced carefully at the hull strength indicator expecting the worst.
jump.66.desc: You continued sitting there at the bottom. Looks like the bathyscaph anchored to the ocean bottom with its own weight had no intention to move. Minutes flew by, you were running out of oxygen. Could this be the end you were destined for, here in deep waters?
jump.68.desc: Suddenly something flashed in the searchlights. You took a closer look and distinctly saw an egg-like silhouette just metres in front of you. "Here it is! I found it!" - you couldn't help the joy. The space alien was made of some strange material with a touch of green bloom to it. You carefully navigated the bathyscaph closer to the strange object that lay still there on the sea-bottom. Now you had to switch on the gripper and carefully snatch the space alien with its powerful oscular probes.
jump.69.desc:
You pushed the button activating the powerful oscular probes of the gripper. Their operation principle was based on the Kalterbruener pseudo-vacuum effect. Down below right under your chair something started buzzing. Through the front illuminator you saw the metal bar with the gripper unbend slowly. Taking over the controls, you started carefully moving the mechanical hands of the robot to the unidentified object. You hit the metal bars on the alien's hull a couple of times, and it seemed to you that it squealed. Finally you managed to put a firm grip on the strange object. Together with the alien you were now pinned down to the bottom. 
- I got it in my gripper. Over. 
You heard a loud applause on the other end of the line. Apparently the entire crew of the rescue base was applauding to you. 
- Excellent. Come back quick! Over and out. - the familiar voice of the captain responded.
Well, time to surface!
jump.71.desc:
You pushed the button activating the powerful oscular probes of the gripper. Their operation principle was based on the Kalterbruener pseudo-vacuum effect. Down below right under your chair something started buzzing. Through the front illuminator you saw the metal bar with the gripper unbend slowly. Taking over the controls, you started carefully moving the mechanical hands of the robot to the unidentified object. You hit the metal bars on the alien's hull a couple of times, and it seemed to you that it squealed. Finally you managed to put a firm grip on the strange object. Together with the alien you were now pinned down to the bottom. 
- I got it in my gripper. Over. - you said into the microphone. 
You did not hear anything in response. Around you there was only the black, oppressing abyss. 
Well, time to surface!
jump.72.text: Get me out of here - quick!
jump.72.desc:
- What?! Are you nuts?! What about the alien? - the captain boomed in resentment.
- What bloody alien! I don't want to die in this abyss! Besides, I am no submariner, I'm a space ranger. I want to go up into space, not down! I promise not to lie ever again and I will honestly kill our enemies! 
- Oh, I see... - the captain said after a long pause: - In that case, drop off the ballast and you'll come up like a cork out of the bottle. Over and out.
jump.73.desc:
- Help-help! - you screamed into the microphone. 
But it was silent. "Strange, - you thought, - I guess I dived too deep! I am doomed to die here in this damned see all alone!"
jump.75.text: Get me out of here - quick!
jump.75.desc: - Didn't you read the documentation? - the voice in the headphones asked. - drop off the ballast and you'll come up like a cork out of the bottle. Over.
jump.76.text: I am running out of oxygen! I am suffocating!
jump.76.desc: - Drop off the ballast and the sea will push you up to the surface. Over.
jump.80.desc: Behind the illuminators it was pitch-dark. Gauge lights flickered softly in the deckhouse and the main engine buzzed quietly. You tried not to think of the icy cold of the multi-metre water layer outside. You tried to relax and leaned back.
jump.82.desc:
Surrounded by the pitch darkness of ocean waters, you wanted to talk to someone.
- Captain. Over.
In response you heard some words, interrupted with loud noises. You could only make out phrase fragments...
- <Ranger>... Do you rea... Over.
- Speak. Can't hear you. Over.
- You... too deep... ...connect... ...be lost... Hold on... 
As if this wasn't enough! Looks like because of the large depth the communication with the rescue team will be lost. Now you were left eye-to-eye with the oceanic abyss! You wish it was all over and you could go back.
jump.84.desc:
- <Ranger>, <Ranger>. Over, - suddenly you heard the captain's voice in the headphones.
- Yes. What is it? Over.
- Looks like we have a problem. The unidentified object kept emitting some signals. I think I told you about that. Now we are noticing the signal is becoming weaker and weaker. By our rough estimates it is going to stop within [p16] minutes. This can mean that the living creature supposedly locked in the object will die. You have little time left, <Ranger>. Try to make it! Over.
- This was not part of the contract! - you exclaimed. - Over.
- I know! - said the captain. - That is why if you manage to get the alien out here alive, we shall pay you an additional  <clr>bonus<clrEnd>. Over.
- I got it. I'll do my best to make it quicker. Over.
 - We sure hope you will. Over and out.
"Yeah right! As if it was not difficult enough", - you thought to yourself.
jump.85.desc: You looked at the clock and understood you were late. Even if there was a living creature there inside, it was surely dead by now. "Well, this way or that, but the capsule must be delivered to the surface - that was the initial objective", - you thought to yourself and continued on the mission.
jump.87.desc:
Suddenly you felt a strong hit. Something flashed in front of the illuminator. 
"What the...!" The hull strength indicator showed considerable damage. "What in the hell was that?"
jump.89.desc:
A strong hit shuddered the entire bathyscaph. Suddenly you saw a scary open maw, riddled with huge caries-stricken teeth, appeared in the illuminator.
- Ye gods!
 -  What is it, <Ranger>? Over, - the response came immediately from the surface.
- There is some huge monster down here! I haven't ever seen anything like that. Even the Dominators look nicer!
- What does it look like? Over.
- It's a got a huge mouth, that is full of teeth, and it's definitely not going to make friends with me. Over.
- Ah... this must be, a monstrodile. A very ancient beast. It is very rare and you can only encounter it at large depths. Behaves very aggressively but it's not as dangerous as it looks. In fact there is very few of them left and they were put in our red black-framed book. You cannot kill them, - the captain informed you.
- Jolly good! Then it will kill me! I wish I were in that book of yours!
- Try to stay calm, - the captain advised. - Most likely, it thinks you dangerous, in fact it is a very peaceful creature. Like any other animal it fears response resistance. Try to scare it away with your searchlights. Over.
- Alright, I'll do my best! That is, if your beast does not eat me before that!
jump.90.desc:
Another strong hit shook the entire bathyscaph. Suddenly you saw a scary open maw, riddled with huge caries-stricken teeth, appeared in the illuminator.
- Ye gods! 
Some scary monster, the ruler of underwater depth, attacked your small ship! The size of his mouth left you no chances. What do you do now? How do you escape that beast?
jump.91.text: I am attacked by a monster!
jump.91.desc:
- What? What does it look like? Over.
- It's a got a huge mouth, that is full of teeth, and it's definitely not going to make friends with me. Over.
- Ah... this must be, a monstrodile. A very ancient beast. It is very rare and you can only encounter it at large depths. Behaves very aggressively but it's not as dangerous as it looks. In fact there is very few of them left and they were put in our red black-framed book. You cannot kill them, - the captain informed you.
- Jolly good! Then it will kill me! I wish I were in that book of yours!
- You should scare him, - the captain advised. - Like any other animal it fears response resistance. Try to scare it away with your searchlights. This should work. Over.
- Alright, I'll do my best! That is, if your beast does not eat me before that!
jump.92.text: I am attacked by a monster!
jump.92.desc:
The headphones responded to you with loud rattling.
- Damn! - you cursed loudly. Then you pronounced a long phrase that made a lot of sense and had a very deep meaning to it. - What should I do now?
You tried frantically to remember the part of the documentation that contained information about the dwellers of the deep - you just started reading that one when the OpSec Department head returned. As far as you could remember it said something about these monsters being afraid of light, and that in fact they were very kind and peaceful creatures.
jump.93.desc: You again felt something hit the ship on the side. How long is it going to last?
jump.94.desc: The underwater beast continued to wriggle around you bathyscaph trying desperately to swallow it. The hits of its huge teeth against the hull did not go unnoticed. Its red-green scales and sharp teeth flashed in the illuminators. <clr>You couldn't get the searchlights in the face of the monstrodile.<clrEnd> You figured you had to turn the apparatus. Would you really have to kiss your life good-bye just because of some prehistoric monster?
jump.95.desc:
The manoeuvre with your searchlights in the face of the monster worked perfectly! You scared the sea beast away. Apparently the ruler of the deep did not expect to meet with return aggression from R I-00-M! It got scared and stopped its attacks. 
- I managed to  scare it away, looks like it finally left me alone! Over, - you reported joyfully to the surface.
- Congrats mate! - you heard the voices of the entire team in the headphones. - Continue on the mission. Over. 
While you were struggling with the prehistoric beast, the bathyscaph got considerably carried away from its main course. Now you will have to correct the direction.
jump.96.desc: The manoeuvre with your searchlights in the face of the monster worked perfectly! You scared the sea beast away. Apparently the ruler of the deep did not expect to meet with return aggression from R I-00-M! It got scared and stopped its attacks. Now you could continue carrying out the mission. While you were struggling with the prehistoric beast, the bathyscaph got considerably carried away from its main course. Now you will have to correct the direction.
jump.97.desc:
Chased by the sea beast, you did notice how you climbed back closer to the surface. Here it suddenly left you alone. (Obviously, the deep-water prehistoric animal did not feel to comfortable up here because of the difference in the pressure.) You let out a sigh of relief, leaned back in your seat, and relaxed. 
- Looks like it's left me alone. I guess it does not like daylight. Over.
- Who doesn't? Over.
- The monster, damn it! An underwater beast! By the way, there was nothing in the contract about monsters, so I will be demanding a bonus, - you responded and switched off the connection.
jump.99.desc: You decided to have some rest, leaned back in your seat and produced a hamburger - courtesy of a Gaalian girl off the "Mermaid" who gave it to you right before the dive. You managed to make very close friends with her, when you accidentally walked into the caboose, while contemplating the coming mission.
jump.100.desc: You figured you could use a short rest - the bathyscaph was moving in the right direction.
jump.114.desc: You dropped the last kilograms that allowed the bathyscaph to sink deeper. After the ship shuddered yet another time you did not notice anything special, but there appeared a flashing sign on the indicator: <clr>Further drop of ballast will cause the ship to start surfacing!<clrEnd>
jump.115.desc:
You felt the already familiar shudder and the ship started climbing up. "Gotta get out of here, before I got squished ", - you thought to yourself and reported in the microphone:
- I am coming up. Over.
In response you heard somebody shout "Bravo!" and some other yells that sounded like cheering.
- Excellent, - you recognised the voice of the captain. - We already prepared everything for your return! Can't wait for you to get up here! Over.
jump.116.desc:
You felt the already familiar shudder and the ship started climbing up. "Gotta get out of here, before I got squished ", - you thought to yourself and reported in the microphone:
- I am coming up. Over.
But no one responded. The feeling of dark solitude overwhelmed you.
jump.117.desc:
You felt the already familiar shudder and the ship started climbing up. "Gotta get out of here, before I got squished ", - you thought to yourself and reported in the microphone:
- I am coming up. Over.
- Good, - you recognised the voice of the captain. - Too bad you did not manage to recover the capsule. We are waiting for you. Over.
jump.118.desc: Another portion of unnecessary cargo started sinking to the bottom. The bathyscaph was rocking from side to side because of the constant ballast drop. The speed of the climb was increasing.
jump.119.desc: The bathyscaph shook slightly and you understood that you hit the ocean bottom. "Right on!" It seemed to you that you saw the rates on the hull strength indicator change.
jump.120.desc: You bathyscaph stayed immobile. Together with the capsule in its gripper, it reminded more of a huge spider clenching its victim. Fish were swimming around you gaily along with some other dwellers of this underwater world, the majority of them rather unusual. Time to get moving!
jump.122.desc: Green scales flashed in the front illuminator. A huge wriggling shadow of some depth dweller loomed over the bathyscaph. This creature was definitely not friendly!
jump.124.desc: A red number lit on the indicator: [p12]. A bit under it you saw another number: "<clr>Max depth:<clrEnd> [p13]". You went to a critical depth! Maybe it's time to drop off the excess ballast and get out of here?
jump.125.desc: Suddenly you saw a light flashing under the air reserve controller. After glancing briefly at the indicator you felt creepy. You had only enough air for another [p15] minutes! "It's getting stuffy..." - you thought.
jump.126.desc:
In the light of the searchlights you saw the bottom of the ocean! You met the sight with much enthusiasm despite the [p12] meters of water over your head.
The bottom was a slope of a rock covered with a thin layer of silt. Some small molluscs danced in the rays of your searchlights. Somewhere not far in this ocean deep lay the space alien. You had to find it as soon as possible!
jump.127.text: What is this R I-00-M thing? Never heard of it
jump.140.text: Alright. I can help you. Where is your bathyscaph?
jump.142.desc: You hardly put your finger near the button, and the turn engines already started working. Excellent assembly quality - hopefully it stays that way!
jump.143.desc: You were so firm in your decision to go south-eastwards that you pushed the button down until it cracked. You got scared - you could break the sensitive Pantel keyboard that way? But no - everything looked fine.
jump.144.desc: This was your favorite direction. Back when you were a kid you enjoyed watching the rising star of your home planet.
jump.145.desc: You pressed the button and the bathyscaph obediently turned in the right direction. You enjoyed navigating this ship, despite the fact that it was much smaller than your spaceship.
jump.146.desc: Thanks to the dropped ballast the bathyscaph managed to rise from the bottom and start drifting. Now you moved constantly scrapping your "belly" against the riff. At times you'd hear the rattling and the bathyscaph shuddered. This could not but affect the hull of the ship.
jump.148.desc: You got rid of yet another portion of the ballast. Now the bathyscaph's will be less.
jump.151.text: I think I reconsidered. I really don't feel like risking my life because of some space alien! There's enough of them up there among the stars, isn't it?! I am going back to the spaceport.
jump.155.desc: The bathyscaph was climbing up. "High-time to get out of here!" You were overwhelmed with joy. Ahead of you there was the surface and a breath of fresh air. "I can't believe it's almost over?!"
jump.158.desc: You heard some squeaking on the right. The hull strength indicator was flashing red. It showed [p20]. Another second and you will be crashed with the thick of the water.
jump.160.text: Tell me more about the co-ordinate system
jump.162.text: Tell me about the bottom relief
jump.164.text: How do I find the object once I'm on the plateau?
jump.166.text: I seem to be a bit on the slow side today... Can you explain to me what is it exactly that you want me to do?!
param.14.crit: You felt that you were losing consciousness. I was becoming impossible to resist the suffocation...
param.19.crit: Just before the water started streaming into the hold, you glanced at the hull strength indicator. It was showing 0 and flashing red...
